subject: Defense notice, evidence handoff, and cost-split for Acme order form

Subject: Initial redlines on indemnity and notice timing

Hi Grace / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our procurement counsel proposed for the Order Form and the indemnity schedule. Two items where we need clarity from legal before procurement can accept:

- Defense control: our standard asks for customer (AcmeCorp) to have defense control for third-party IP claims with the right to select counsel; we understand Redwood prefers defend-and-control for commercial third-party claims — can you confirm what you can accept for Order Form level?
- Notice & evidence timeline: procurement insists on a 30-day notice window and an explicit evidence-sharing SLA (how/where evidence will be staged).

We included a suggested cost-split clause for settlements (see paragraph 3.2). Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept a limited-cost-split (Redwood pays direct damages up to cap; thereafter 50/50 split) or require full defense reimbursement?

Please see attached: Acme_OrderForm_Redlines_20270525.pdf

Goal: get a narrow set of legal positions we can push to our GC and move to procurement sign-off this coming Friday.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Procurement, AcmeCorp

Jane — thanks, and appreciated the clear asks. Looping Kimberly (legal) and Ben (sales) to align on negotiable items. High-level from product/sales:

- We are open to a defend-vs-reimburse compromise for the Order Form but need defined guardrails on notice/evidence and a short cure window to evaluate technical remediation.
- Quant caps: we can accept the proposed order-form cap tied to the purchase value for the first contract year; beyond that we need to revert to MSA caps.

Kimberly — can you propose redline language for: (a) defense control / counsel selection compromise, (b) explicit notice timeline and evidence staging obligations, and (c) settlement approval process and cost-split mechanics? I attached Acme's redlines for reference.

Attachment: Proposed_Notice_Workflow_20270526.docx

—Grace

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines on indemnity and notice timing

Grace / Ben / Jane — thanks for the context. Draft positions below (high level), with suggested redline snippets. I pasted the operative bits inline to keep the thread clear.

1) Defense control / counsel selection (compromise):
"Redwood shall have the right to assume control of the defense of any third-party claim alleging IP infringement; provided, however, that Customer may elect to assume control by providing written notice within 10 days of receipt of claim and shall use counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood. If Customer assumes control, Redwood shall have the right to participate at its own expense."

Rationale: preserves Redwood's ability to manage technical defense while giving Acme a short window to opt in.

2) Notice & evidence SLA:
"Customer shall provide written notice of any claim promptly and in any event within 30 days of becoming aware. Customer shall make commercially reasonable efforts to stage evidence (logs, sample prompts, model identifiers) on a secure shared repository within 15 calendar days of notice; Redwood shall provide a secure intake workflow and designate an evidence custodian within 5 business days of notice."

Rationale: aligns with Acme's 30-day ask but keeps timelines operationally feasible.

3) Settlement & cost-split mechanics:
"Where Redwood elects to defend and obtains a settlement or judgment, Redwood shall have authority to settle such claim; if Customer elects to assume defense control pursuant to Section X, any settlement that would materially bind Redwood shall require Redwood's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. For settlement amounts exceeding the applicable contract cap, parties agree to equally share amounts in excess of the cap up to a negotiated ceiling of $1,000,000, unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Rationale: provides a 50/50 excess split but limits Redwood exposure above a negotiated ceiling.

Please note: these are starting positions. If Acme requires counsel selection exclusively in the customer's hands for all claims, we would need to increase the order-form cap or take an insurance-first approach.

Action items: Ben, can you confirm commercial tradeoffs (willingness to increase cap or accept excess-split) so I can finalize redlines? Jane, if you can confirm whether your GC needs counsel selection exclusivity we can triage alternatives (insurance, escrow).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Jane — quick note to keep momentum:

- Kimberly's language is a reasonable compromise. From a commercial perspective Redwood can accept the 50/50 split on amounts exceeding the contract cap up to the $1,000,000 ceiling Kimberly proposed, provided we keep the 10-day customer election window and counsel participation rights.
- We can offer a one-off increase to the order-form cap (20% uplift) if Acme insists on exclusive counsel selection for any IP claim; otherwise we prefer the defend-and-control default.

Proposed next steps:
